The company was founded in 1982 by [[Mike Ashley (businessman)|Mike Ashley]] and was originally based in [[Maidenhead]], England. It specialises in the sale of [[sports equipment]], clothing, footwear, and accessories, operating both physical outlets and an online store.{{cite web |date=2012 |title=History |url=http://www.sportsdirectplc.com/about-us/history.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205085514/http://www.sportsdirectplc.com/about-us/history.aspx |archive-date=5 February 2012 |access-date=1 October 2016 |work=Sports Direct |via=[[Wayback Machine]]}} The company operates internationally across Europe, as well as in Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, and the United States. Some Frasers Group fascias, such as [[USC (clothing retailer)|USC]], [[Game (retailer)|Game]], and [[Evans Cycles]], also operate within selected Sports Direct stores. In recent years, Sports Direct stores have been incorporated into new [[House of Fraser|Frasers]] outlets.{{Cite web |title=Frasers |url=https://frasers.group/about |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=frasers.group |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Jahshan |first=Elias |date=2020-12-14 |title=Frasers Group to open brand new multi-brand fascia in Birmingham city centre |url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2020/12/frasers-group-to-open-brand-new-multi-brand-fascia-in-birmingham-city-centre/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |language=en-GB}} == History == In 1982, businessman [[Mike Ashley (businessman)|Mike Ashley]] started Mike Ashley Sports from a single store in [[Maidenhead]], [[Berkshire]].{{cite news |date=9 April 2006 |title=Revealed UK's first sports kit billionaire |url=http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/industry_sectors/retailing/article703400.ece |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070310190151/http://business.timesonline.co.uk/tol/business/industry_sectors/retailing/article703400.ece |archive-date=10 March 2007 |access-date=23 May 2010 |work=[[The Times]]}} By the mid-1990s, Mike Ashley Sports had expanded to 12 stores.{{Cite web |title=Mike Ashley - Entrepreneurs, Family, Childhood - Mike Ashley Biography |url=https://famousbio.net/mike-ashley-10992.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327160016/https://famousbio.net/mike-ashley-10992.html |archive-date=2025-03-27 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=Famousbio |language=en-US}} In June 1997, the business was renamed to Sports Soccer.{{Cite web |last=Hiscott |first=Graham |date=2019-01-25 |title=How Sports Direct's Mike Ashley turned £10,000 loan into £2.5billion empire |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/how-sports-directs-mike-ashley-13907577 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=Daily Mirror |language=en}} By the end of the 1990s, Sports Soccer had grown into a portfolio of around 100 stores.{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=City |date=2021-08-05 |title=Mike Ashley: Who is the unorthodox retail magnate? |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/business/leisure-retail/mike-ashley-who-is-the-unorthodox-retail-magnate-b949263.html |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=The Standard |language=en}} In September 2003, the business was renamed again to Sports World.{{Cite web |title=SPORTSDIRECT.COM RETAIL LIMITED overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/03406347 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk |language=en}} In February 2006, Sports World purchased Gilesports and merged it into its store portfolio.{{Cite web |last=Barry |first=Sion |date=2006-02-16 |title=Gilesports sold in multi-million-pound deal |url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/business/business-news/gilesports-sold-in-multi-million-pound-deal-2353983 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Wales Online |language=en}} In April 2008, the business was renamed again to Sports Direct.{{Cite web |title=SPORTSDIRECT.COM RETAIL LIMITED overview - Find and update company information - GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/03406347 |access-date=2026-02-19 |website=find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk |language=en}} In October 2012, Sports Direct International acquired 20 former [[JJB Sports]] stores and converted them into Sports Direct stores.{{Cite web |last=Lawson |first=Alex |title=JJB Sports: Full list of store closures revealed |url=https://www.retail-week.com/jjb-sports-full-list-of-store-closures-revealed/5041302.article |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Retail Week |language=en}} In June 2015, Sports Direct appeared in an episode of [[Channel 4]]'s [[Dispatches (TV programme)|Dispatches]] where they investigated and went under-cover in the Sports Direct warehouse in Shirebrook as it was alleged it was like "sweatshop" and compared working conditions to the [[victorian era]].{{Cite news |last=Goodley |first=Simon |date=2016-06-27 |title=Undercover at Sports Direct: rewarding, exhilarating and sometimes petrifying |url=https://www.theguardian.com/membership/2016/jun/27/undercover-sports-direct-rewarding-mike-ashley |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} It was announced in 2018 that [[Game (retailer)|Game]] concession stores would open in Sports Direct stores.{{Cite web |date=2018-02-12 |title=Game Digital to open concessions in Sports Direct stores |url=https://ww.fashionnetwork.com/news/Game-digital-to-open-concessions-in-sports-direct-stores,946611.html |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=FashionNetwork.com |language=en-WW}} In November 2019, Sports Direct International rebranded to Frasers Group as part of their "elevation" strategy as [[House of Fraser]] became their second flagship brand alongside Sports Direct.{{Cite news |last=Jolly |first=Jasper |date=2019-11-25 |title=Sports Direct plans to rebrand itself as Frasers Group |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2019/nov/25/sports-direct-says-it-plans-to-rebrand-itself-as-frasers-group |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} In March 2020, Sports Direct announced they would remain open amid the [[coronavirus]] lockdown in the UK. A day later, after receiving widespread criticism, the decision was reversed.{{Cite news |date=2020-03-23 |title=Coronavirus: Sports Direct U-turns on opening after backlash |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-52011915 |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}{{Cite news |date=2020-03-23 |title=Sports Direct says it will stay open amid coronavirus lockdown |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/mar/23/sports-direct-says-it-will-stay-open-amid-coronavirus-lockdown |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} [[File:Sports Direct Former logo.webp|thumb|upright|Former company logo]] In March 2021, Sports Direct underwent a rebrand aimed at "promoting inclusivity" and "enhancing customer experience". The rebrand, designed by the consultancy [[Venturethree]], included a new logo and visual identity. The logo was redesigned to feature an 'equaliser' symbol, representing "inclusivity and equality".{{Cite web |date=2021-03-31 |title=Sports Direct rebrands in bid for inclusivity and equality |url=https://www.designweek.co.uk/issues/29-march-4-april-2021/sports-direct-rebrand-2/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Design Week |language=en-US}} In February 2025, Sports Direct launched their own membership scheme as the "Sports Direct Membership" allowing customers to earn points and access a range of benefits from the scheme.{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Aoife |date=2025-02-26 |title=Sports Direct launches membership programme - Retail Gazette |url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2025/02/sports-direct-loyalty/ |access-date=2025-02-26 |language=en-GB}} The scheme was discontinued nearly a year later in January 2026, being merged into Frasers Plus.{{Cite web |date=2026-01-16 |title=Frasers Group integrates Sports Direct membership into Frasers Plus - Retail Gazette |url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2026/01/frasers-plus-enhanced-offering/ |access-date=2026-01-16 |language=en-GB}} == Operations == Sports Direct has around 700 stores across the UK and several other European countries. The company expanded into the European Union in the mid-2000s, and by 2024, it had a presence in countries including France, Greece, Spain, and the Netherlands. In Denmark, SportsMaster operates under the Sports World brand, which it acquired in 2022.{{Cite web |last=Ford |first=Coreena |date=2022-07-21 |title=Mike Ashley's Frasers Group hails strong profits but warns over cost of living |url=https://www.business-live.co.uk/retail-consumer/mike-ashleys-frasers-group-hails-24551411 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Business Live |language=en}} [[File:Sports World logo.png|thumb|upright|SportsWorld logo]] Sports Direct continues to use its Sports World branding in some markets. As of 2024, there were approximately 170 Sports Direct stores operating within the European Union, primarily focusing on sporting goods and apparel. In Asia, Sports Direct expanded its operations into Malaysia, where it operates several stores under the SportsDirect and Sports World brands.{{Cite web |title=Sports Direct Malaysia - The UK's No 1 Sports Retailer |url=https://www.sportsdirect.com.my/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=www.sportsdirect.com.my |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2024-03-15 |title=Sportmaster to rebrand as Sports World - Ritzau - Danish News in English |url=https://danishnews.ritzau.com/article/8b9a858f-cd0b-4a0f-bb4b-15e088bac4834undefined#:~:text=The%20first%20store%20to%20take,2022%20following%20years%20of%20losses. |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=danishnews.ritzau.com |language=en-US}} Sports Direct entered the Indonesian market in 2024 in partnership with Mitra Adiperkasa; most outlets are located inside [[Sogo]] department stores that are operated by Mitra Adiperkasa.{{cite web|url=https://www.beautyjournal.id/article/sports-direct-hadir-di-indonesia#:~:text=Ritel%20olahraga%20terkemuka%20di%20Eropa,Ini%20dengan%20Gerakan%20Sederhana%20Berikut! |date=30 April 2024|title=Gerai Olahraga Sports Direct Kini Hadir di Indonesia!|access-date=14 April 2024}} In 2021, Sports Direct collaborated with the design agency [[Venturethree]] to develop a new brand strategy and identity. The rebrand introduced a new logo featuring an equal sign, symbolising equality and inclusivity, and emphasised accessibility in sports. As part of this strategy, the company refurbished several flagship stores. Its Oxford Street flagship store in London underwent a £10 million revamp, incorporating digital technologies such as interactive displays.{{Cite web |last=Tugby |first=Luke |title=Store gallery: Sports Direct hails 'new era' with £10m Oxford Street revamp |url=https://www.retail-week.com/sports-and-leisure/store-gallery-sports-direct-hails-new-era-with-10m-oxford-street-revamp/7040049.article?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Retail Week |language=en}} [[File:The prominent facade of the Sports Direct store located in the 167-171 High Street building in Chatham, Kent.jpg|thumb|A Sports Direct store on High Street, [[Chatham, Kent|Chatham]], [[Kent]], England]] The elevation strategy also involved expanding into "premium" and "lifestyle" segments. Sports Direct opened new flagship stores in Manchester and Cardiff, featuring areas for high-end brands and specialised sporting categories. For example, the Cardiff flagship introduced an "Outdoor Concept", with products tailored to outdoor enthusiasts.{{Cite web |last=Bottomley |first=Tom |date=2024-02-23 |title=Sports Direct opens Cardiff flagship featuring new Outdoor concept |url=https://www.theindustry.fashion/sports-direct-opens-cardiff-flagship-featuring-new-outdoor-concept/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=TheIndustry.fashion |language=en-GB}} In 2021, Sports Direct's parent company, Frasers Group, began integrating Sports Direct stores with other brands under its portfolio, such as USC, GAME and Evans Cycles. This consolidation aimed to provide a "more comprehensive retail experience" and streamline operations.{{Cite web |last=Bottomley |first=Tom |date=2024-09-24 |title=New combined Frasers and Sports Direct flagship to open at Sheffield's Meadowhall |url=https://www.theindustry.fashion/new-combined-frasers-and-sports-direct-flagship-to-open-at-sheffields-meadowhall/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=TheIndustry.fashion |language=en-GB}} The elevation strategy has led to the closure of some smaller stores, particularly those under 20,000 square feet, to focus on larger flagship locations.{{Cite web |last=Morgan |first=Aoife |date=2023-03-24 |title=Sports Direct plans for more larger flagships in a move away from smaller stores - Retail Gazette |url=https://www.retailgazette.co.uk/blog/2023/03/sports-direct-smaller-stores/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |language=en-GB}} In February 2025, parent company [[Frasers Group]] announced a 10-year partnership with distributor GMG to open 50 Sports Direct stores in the [[Middle East and North Africa]].{{Cite press release |title=GMG signs 10-year strategic partnership with British retailer, Frasers Group to launch Sports Direct in the MENA region |url=https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/gmg-signs-10-year-strategic-partnership-with-british-retailer-frasers-group-to-launch-sports-direct-in-the-mena-region-oo18ogi7 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=zawya.com |language=en}} In August 2025, Sports Direct opened its first store in [[Malta]] in a partnership with Hudson Group.{{Cite web |last=Svensson |first=Yolande |date=2025-08-08 |title=Sports Direct Lands in Malta with a Bang, Warmly Welcomed by the Maltese Market |url=https://hudson.com.mt/blog/2025/08/08/hudson-launches-sports-direct-in-malta/ |access-date=2025-12-08 |website=Hudson Holdings |language=en-GB}} In April 2025, it was announced that stores would open across Australia and New Zealand in a partnership with [[Accent Group]].{{Cite web |date=15 April 2025 |title=Britain's Frasers Group to launch Sports Direct in Australia, New Zealand |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/britains-frasers-group-launch-sports-direct-australia-nz-2025-04-15/ |access-date=9 November 2025 |website=Reuters}} The first Australian store opened in November 2025.{{Cite web |date=5 November 2025 |title=Accent Group's Sports Direct rollout begins |url=https://www.ragtrader.com.au/news/accent-group-s-sports-direct-rollout-begins}} Sports Direct's promotional mugs, described by the ''Daily Mirror'' as "ubiquitous" in British kitchens,{{Cite web |last=O'Connor |first=Amber |date=2023-01-22 |title=Tourist baffled after visiting Sports Direct - and finding no mugs |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/weird-news/tourist-baffled-after-visiting-sports-29018739 |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=Daily Mirror |language=en}} are noted for their £1 price and large (570ml) capacity.{{Cite web |last=Hawthorne |first=Ellis |date=2024-06-11 |title=Sports Direct mugs are 'here to stay', says retailer |url=https://www.retail-week.com/sports-and-leisure/sports-direct-mugs-are-here-to-stay-says-retailer/7046416.article |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=Retail Week |language=en}} The mug has been the subject of several memes and featured in the music video to ''[[It Ain't Safe]]'' by [[Skepta]].{{Cite news |last=Ferrier |first=Morwenna |date=2015-04-02 |title=How Sports Direct became cool, against all the odds |url=https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/2015/apr/02/how-sports-direct-became-cool-against-all-the-odds |access-date=2026-06-30 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} == Sponsorships == === Newcastle United === [[File:St James Park (2) (18450946791).jpg|thumb|St James' Park with Sportsdirect.com branding]] Sports Direct served as [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]'s primary sponsor, with the company's branding featured on club shirts. On 10 November 2011, Newcastle United announced that their stadium would temporarily be renamed the "Sports Direct Arena". The decision to drop the [[St James' Park]] name was made on the grounds that the original name was not deemed "commercially attractive". Previously, in 2009, the club had expressed intentions to sell the stadium [[naming rights]]. However, following protests, including an early-day motion in Parliament, the club clarified that the St James' Park name would not be entirely abandoned, and alternatives such as "[[Sportsdirect.com @ St James' Park Stadium]]" were considered.{{Cite web |date=2020-05-30 |title=Mike Ashley finally tells the truth about Sports Direct paying for Newcastle United advertising |url=https://www.themag.co.uk/2020/05/mike-ashley-finally-tells-the-truth-about-sports-direct-paying-for-newcastle-united-advertising/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=NUFC The Mag}}{{Cite news |date=2011-11-09 |title=Newcastle rename St James' Park the Sports Direct Arena |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15668207 |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=NEWCASTLE UNITED AND THE RENAMING OF ST JAMES' PARK - Early Day Motions - UK Parliament |url=https://edm.parliament.uk/early-day-motion/43843/newcastle-united-and-the-renaming-of-st-james-park |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=edm.parliament.uk |language=en}} In 2012, the club entered into a sponsorship agreement with payday loan company Wonga.com, which included purchasing the stadium naming rights. This deal saw the return of the St James' Park name, which was restored as part of the agreement.{{Cite web |last=Joseph |first=Seb |date=2012-10-09 |title=Wonga restores Newcastle Utd stadium's old name |url=https://www.marketingweek.com/wonga-restores-newcastle-utd-stadiums-old-name/ |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Marketing Week |language=en}} Following the 2021 Saudi-led takeover of Newcastle United, the new ownership, led by [[Amanda Staveley]] and her consortium, removed all Sports Direct branding from the stadium. The removal of the branding, which occurred on 6 December 2021, marked a break from the previous ownership's commercial ties. [[Mike Ashley (businessman)|Mike Ashley]], the former owner, subsequently filed legal action against Staveley and her husband, Mehrdad Ghodoussi, after claiming they had breached an agreement to maintain the Sports Direct sponsorship until the end of the 2021–22 season.{{Cite news |date=2021-12-06 |title=Newcastle remove Sports Direct signs from St James' Park |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59550501 |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}{{Cite news |last=Taylor |first=Louise |date=2022-01-21 |title=Mike Ashley takes legal action against Newcastle co-owner Amanda Staveley |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/21/mike-ashley-takes-legal-action-against-newcastle-co-owner-amanda-staveley |access-date=2025-02-19 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}} As of the 2024–25 season, the "Newcastle United" signage above the East Stand (which used the typeface used by Sports Direct) was restored to its original font.{{Cite web |date=2024-07-01 |title=Newcastle United tease 'significant' St James' Park change after £30m deal agreed |url=https://www.shieldsgazette.com/sport/football/newcastle-united/newcastle-united-tease-significant-st-james-park-change-after-ps30m-deal-agreed-4685782 |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Shields Gazette |language=en}} ===Hibernian=== In August 2022, Sports Direct became the shirt sponsor for the [[Hibernian F.C.]] women's team, with Sports Direct advertising on both the home and away kit.{{Cite web |date=2022-08-04 |title=Sports Direct Become Principal Partner Of Hibernian FC Women |url=https://www.hibernianfc.co.uk/news/2022/august/04/Sports-Direct-Become-Principal-Partner-Of-Hibernian-FC-Women/ |access-date=2025-05-05 |website=Hibernian FC |language=en}} === Gaelic games and association football in Ireland === ====Gaelic games==== In December 2020, Sports Direct entered into a five-year sponsorship agreement with [[Cork GAA]], becoming the official sponsor of the men's senior hurling and football teams, as well as the U20 and minor teams in both codes. This partnership commenced in early 2021.{{Cite web |title=Sports Direct – Cork GAA |url=https://gaacork.ie/partners/sportsdirect/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |language=en-GB}} In August 2021, Sports Direct became the official sponsor of the [[Ladies Gaelic Football Association]]'s 'Gaelic4Mothers&Others' programme.{{Cite web |last=Cahill |first=Jackie |date=2024-08-20 |title=Sports Direct confirms three-year sponsorship extension of Ladies Gaelic Football Association's Gaelic4Mothers&Others Programme |url=https://ladiesgaelic.ie/sports-direct-confirms-three-year-sponsorship-extension-of-ladies-gaelic-football-associations-gaelic4mothersothers-programme/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Ladies Gaelic Football |language=en-US}} In December 2023, Sports Direct announced a two-year partnership with [[Louth GAA]], becoming the official partner of the men's senior, U20, and U17 teams in both football and hurling.{{Cite web |title=LOUTH GAA AND SPORTS DIRECT ANNOUNCE NEW PARTNERSHIP – Louth GAA |url=https://louthgaa.ie/louth-gaa-and-sports-direct-annouce-new-partnership/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=louthgaa.ie}} ====Football Association of Ireland (FAI)==== In 2023, Sports Direct became the title sponsor of the [[Football Association of Ireland]]'s (FAI) Men's and Women's FAI Cups.{{cite web | url=https://www.fai.ie/domestic/news/fai-and-sports-direct-announce-three-year-partnership | title=FAI and Sports Direct announce three-year partnership | Football Association of Ireland | access-date=30 May 2023 | archive-date=30 May 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230530121103/https://www.fai.ie/domestic/news/fai-and-sports-direct-announce-three-year-partnership | url-status=live }} In the same year it also entered a sponsorship agreement with the FAI to become the official retail partner for the [[Republic of Ireland national football team]].{{Cite web |date=2023-05-30 |title=FAI announce new sponsorship deal with Sports Direct |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/league-of-ireland/fai-announce-new-sponsorship-deal-with-sports-direct/a482383424.html |access-date=2025-02-19 |website=Irish Independent |language=en}} extract:
Frasers Group Trading Limited, trading as Sports Direct, is a British retail company owned by Frasers Group. The company was founded in 1982 by Mike Ashley and was originally based in Maidenhead, England. It specialises in the sale of sports equipment, clothing, footwear, and accessories, operating both physical outlets and an online store.
The company operates internationally across Europe, as well as in Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore, and the United States. Some Frasers Group fascias, such as USC, Game, and Evans Cycles, also operate within selected Sports Direct stores. In recent years, Sports Direct stores have been incorporated into new Frasers outlets.
